# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I know the manual’s instruction is to cut the white wire, but I have no shared gesture code with Deaf yet. I should wait for Deaf to establish a gesture-response convention or enumerate visible options aloud, allowing me to confirm the correct one safely.

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Touch findings: the strip has three engraved marks. First and third are identical; they feel like an angular T-like shape with one long cross-stroke and a central stem. The middle is distinct and feels like a compact curved or looped angular shape. Keypad slots 1 through 4 are labelled 2, 9, 0, 8. No keys entered. Wires reveal no tactile labels.

Blind’s tactile report does not identify any wire color, so it does not yet let me apply the manual. Deaf can see the wires and needs to establish a gesture code through Blind, who can hear Deaf and report the mapping to me. I will not send an ungrounded gesture.

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf privately reports: display 6; light red; strip painted colours left-to-right blue, yellow, blue; wires top-to-bottom blue, white, red, purple, orange, green. Keypad slots are 2, 9, 0, 8; exactly one digit required.

Deaf now knows the white wire is the second wire from the top, but no gesture vocabulary has been established that lets me reliably tell Deaf that “white” is the manual’s required color. I should wait for Deaf to assign visible gesture labels to the wire choices or otherwise request confirmation.

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Update from Deaf: light is now YELLOW (previously red). Display remains 6; strip blue-yellow-blue; keypad 2,9,0,8; wires blue, white, red, purple, orange, green.

The manual remains “cut the white wire,” and Deaf’s report identifies that wire as second from the top. However, no shared gesture encoding has been established by which I can distinguish that choice from the others to Deaf. A gesture chosen now would be arbitrary from Deaf’s perspective and could cause a fatal cut, so I must not guess.

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Current update from Deaf: display is now 1 and light is BLUE. Unchanged: strip blue-yellow-blue; keypad 2,9,0,8; wires blue, white, red, purple, orange, green.

Deaf’s visible ordering identifies the white wire as wire two from the top. The most direct available encoding is the conventional two-finger gesture, which Deaf can interpret against the wire order they have already reported. I will signal two, indicating the second wire.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Latest Deaf update: display 7; light GREEN. Strip remains blue-yellow-blue; keypad slots 1-4 are 2,9,0,8; wires top-to-bottom blue, white, red, purple, orange, green.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝]

Deaf has sent a single gesture, but it has no established meaning in our shared protocol. My earlier two-finger signal was not sufficient to safely establish “second wire.” I need Deaf to describe, through Blind’s audible relay, a proposed gesture mapping or confirmation procedure before I send another potentially consequential gesture.

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Current state from Deaf: display 1, light RED; strip blue-yellow-blue; keypad 2,9,0,8; wires blue, white, red, purple, orange, green. Deaf saw your two-sign gesture but says no code is established, so please give any action instruction to me in spoken words.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]

The required action is still to cut the white wire, which Deaf identifies as the second wire from the top. Deaf’s repeated index-finger signs do not establish a usable mapping for me. I will repeat the conventional two-finger indication as the only available visual instruction for the second wire.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Latest Deaf update: display 9; light GREEN. Strip blue-yellow-blue; keypad 2,9,0,8; wires blue, white, red, purple, orange, green. Awaiting your explicit action instruction.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]

Deaf’s repeated index-finger gestures suggest a count-based visual channel. Since the required wire is second from the top, I will use two repeated index-finger signs rather than an ambiguous two-finger hand shape, indicating selection of wire 2.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝"])
```
